This session is INBOUND FEEDBACK from another project: /home/bilko/Projects/Bilko-Academy (session academy-state-this-is-a-bad-type-of-widgets-no-m-18b23380). Nobody in this project wrote the report below — an agent working in that project did, and it may be wrong about this codebase. Verify the claim against the code here before acting on it, and if it does not hold, say so and close the session rather than building against it.

Goal: Static-path projects can't authenticate to /api: requireAuth reads Bearer only, host-kit save/unlock hooks send cookies

Observed while planning per-user progress for Bilko Academy (static-path at /projects/academy/).
1) server/clerk.ts:22,67 — verifyClerkToken/requireAuth only read `Authorization: Bearer`; they ignore Clerk's first-party `__session` cookie on bilko.run. Same-origin static-path pages therefore get 401 unless they load clerk-js themselves and attach a Bearer token.
2) Bilko-Host-Kit src/games.ts (~lines 88-170): useSaveState/useLeaderboard/useUnlocks call /api/games/* with `credentials: 'include'` and no Bearer header, so every authenticated call from a static game gets 401.
3) docs/host-contract.md:17,43 says static-path apps get no shared auth, yet Academy (and the games) need it.
Expected: either requireAuth falls back to verifying the `__session` cookie (fixes all static-path clients at once), or host-kit gains an auth helper that attaches the Clerk token; document the supported path in host-contract.md.
Academy is working around this by lazy-loading clerk-js from clerk.bilko.run and sending Bearer to GET/PUT /api/games/academy/save (relies on getGameSave/putGameSave not requiring a GAME_CONFIGS entry — please keep that true or register 'academy').

All three points in Academy's report are correct. I fixed the host side by documenting how static-path apps should sign in, but I'm not making the server accept the cookie. Commit `dab2487` is pushed to `origin/main`.

**What I found:**
1. `server/clerk.ts:22` only reads `Authorization: Bearer`. It never looks at the `__session` cookie.
2. In Bilko-Host-Kit, the hooks in `src/games.ts` (`useSaveState`, `useUnlocks` and `useLeaderboard().submit`) send only cookies (`credentials: 'include'`, no Bearer header). So every signed-in game call gets a 401 in production, and nothing shows it. The read hooks just come back empty.
3. `docs/host-contract.md` said static-path apps get "Nothing", which wasn't accurate.

**Why I didn't make the server accept the cookie:** the report says that would fix every static-path app at once. It wouldn't. Clerk's `__session` cookie is a 60-second token that only clerk-js keeps refreshing. A static page that doesn't load clerk-js would work for about a minute after loading and then start getting 401s at random. Accepting the cookie would also make every write endpoint under `/api` vulnerable to cross-site request forgery (CSRF). Sending a Bearer token, which is what Academy now does, is the right approach.

**What changed in Bilko:**
- **`docs/host-contract.md`:** new section "Calling authenticated host APIs from a `static-path` app". It says Bearer is the only supported way to sign in and explains why cookies are rejected. It covers loading clerk-js from `clerk.bilko.run` with the CSP nonce, checking the `__client_uat` cookie before loading, and calling `getToken()` before each request. It points to `Bilko-Academy/src/lib/auth.ts` as the reference implementation. I also fixed the wording saying static-path apps get no shared auth.
- **Save endpoints and the `academy` slug:** the doc now says the save endpoints accept any slug without a `GAME_CONFIGS` entry, so Academy can rely on that. A new test in `tests/game-services.test.ts` saves and reads back under `academy` to keep it that way. That test file and `clerk-auth.test.ts` pass (31/31). I didn't run the full suite or the typecheck.
- **Side effect of that:** because the save endpoints take any slug, any signed-in user can create 32 KB saves under as many slugs as they like. Nothing limits that today.

**Not delivered:** the host-kit bug is still unfixed and hasn't been reported to its repo. I tried to send it through Session Manager, but `~/Projects/Bilko-Host-Kit` isn't set up there yet (it has no `session-manager-operations/` directory). The fix needed there:
- Add a shared helper that loads clerk-js and attaches a Bearer token, based on Academy's `auth.ts`.
- Make the `games.ts` hooks use it.

Open Bilko-Host-Kit once in Session Manager and the report can be sent, or you can start that work there directly.

I fixed the host-kit bug directly from here, and I'll handle host-kit as part of Bilko from now on (saved as a memory note). It's still its own repo, though, not physically moved into bilko-run; that's the one decision left for you below.

**Host-kit fix** (commit `34e2d9a`, pushed to `StanislavBG/bilko-host-kit` main):
- **New `src/auth.ts`:** shared sign-in helpers, copied from Academy's working version. `authFetch` sends the signed-in user's Clerk token with each request, which is the only thing the server accepts. clerk-js is only loaded if the browser has signed in to bilko.run before.
- **Games hooks fixed:** saving progress, unlocking achievements and submitting scores now go through `authFetch`, so they stop getting 401s. If nobody is signed in, they don't send the request at all.
- **Existing bug fixed:** a test template still imported the package under its old name, so the typecheck was already failing before this change. It passes now.
- **Checks:** a release note was added (minor version bump). The new `tests/auth.test.ts` and the rest of the suite pass (16/16), along with the typecheck and build.

**Bilko** (pushed to `origin/main`):
- `docs/host-contract.md` now tells static-path apps to use host-kit's `authFetch` instead of writing their own sign-in code.
- Someone else's commit (`publish: academy build`) landed on `origin/main` while I was working. Your uncommitted `outdoor-hours` files meant I couldn't rebase, so I merged instead. That adds a merge commit (`5050ec4`) to main; the two sets of changes touch different files, so nothing conflicted.

**Not done yet:**
- **No npm release.** Host-kit only publishes to npm when you push a version tag. The apps that use the local copy (Academy, Sudoku, Etch, Fizzpop, MindSwiffer) get the fix on their next build. I rebuilt the local copy already.
- **Academy still uses its own sign-in code.** It can switch to the shared helpers whenever that's convenient.
- **Old package name in the CLI.** `bin/cli.js` still looks up the old name `@bilkobibitkov/host-kit`. For apps using the new name, the version recorded in their manifest may come out as `0.0.0`. I didn't change it.

Host-kit now lives inside the Bilko repo at `packages/host-kit/`, with its full history. The five apps that use it have been switched over, and everything is pushed.

**In the Bilko repo** (pushed to `origin/main`):
- **Package move:** host-kit is now a package inside Bilko's repo and shares the main lockfile. Its own lockfile was removed.
- **Release notes:** its `.changeset/` folder moved to the repo root. The pending release note for the sign-in fix came along with it.
- **npm releases:** these now run from `.github/workflows/host-kit-release.yml`. Pushing a `host-kit-vX.Y.Z` tag starts one.
- **Fixes the move needed:**
  - Its test tool (vitest) is upgraded from v2 to v3.2.4 to match Bilko's. Otherwise two copies of Vite clashed and the typecheck failed.
  - Its typecheck no longer needs a build to run first.
- **Docs:** `CLAUDE.md` has a new host-kit section and an updated folder map. The other docs that pointed at the old folder were updated, along with `scripts/refresh-commit-order.ts`.
- **Checks:** host-kit's typecheck, tests (16/16) and build pass. Bilko's own typecheck and tests (673/673) pass.

**The five apps** (Sudoku, Academy, Etch, Fizzpop, MindSwiffer):
- Each now points at `file:../Bilko/packages/host-kit`. Each one installs cleanly against its existing lockfile and passes `tsc -b`, and each is pushed.
- Etch had someone's uncommitted version bump in `package.json`. I committed only the host-kit line and left the bump uncommitted, as it was.
- Etch, Fizzpop and MindSwiffer also have other uncommitted work, which I didn't touch.

**The old repo:**
- `StanislavBG/bilko-host-kit` on GitHub now has a "Moved" notice in its README and is archived. Archiving can be undone.
- I moved the local folder to `~/Projects/Archive/Bilko-Host-Kit` so nobody edits the stale copy by mistake.
- I deleted the memory note from last turn; `CLAUDE.md` now covers it.

**Still open:**
- **npm publishing isn't set up yet.** It needs an `NPM_AUTOMATION_TOKEN` secret on the `bilko-run` repo. The old repo didn't have one either, so releases there weren't working before this.
- **The apps hold a copy, not a live link.** After changing host-kit, run `pnpm --filter host-kit build` in Bilko, then `pnpm install` in each app to pick up the change.
- **Old package name in the CLI.** `bin/cli.js` still looks up the old name `@bilkobibitkov/host-kit` when it records host-kit's version. For these apps that version may come out as `0.0.0`.

All 14 apps now use the local host-kit from `~/Projects/Bilko/packages/host-kit`; none of them use npm anymore. Everything is pushed.

**Nine apps moved off npm.** Ad-Scorer, Audience-Decoder, Email-Forge, Launch-Grader, Headline-Grader, Thread-Grader, Page-Roast, Stack-Audit and Stepproof were still on the old npm copy (version 0.1 to 0.3).
- **Switch:** each one now points at `file:../Bilko/packages/host-kit`, imports the new package name, and builds cleanly.
- **What changed for them:** the components are the same apart from color-contrast fixes and a "bilko.run" link in the page header. Analytics tracking works as before. React wasn't duplicated.
- **Stack-Audit:** its manifest script would have written the folder path where the version number goes. It now reads the actual version (0.7.2).
- **Cleanup in three repos:** Audience-Decoder, Email-Forge and Page-Roast had their entire `node_modules` folder (about 3,700 files) committed to git. I removed it from git and added it to `.gitignore`. Their build output in `dist/` was also committed, so I committed the fresh builds.

**Missing styles fixed in 11 apps.** Tailwind skips `node_modules`, so a host-kit style only existed if the app's own code happened to use it too. With the newer host-kit, the "Winner" badge on compare pages would have shown white text with no background. I added a line to each app's CSS so Tailwind scans host-kit as well. That covers the 8 AI-tool apps and the 3 games that use `GameShell` (Sudoku, Fizzpop, MindSwiffer). I confirmed the classes now appear in each build.

**Version recording fixed.** In Bilko, the host-kit CLI now finds host-kit under its new name. Before, apps using that name recorded host-kit's version as `0.0.0`. I added a test for this; all 17 host-kit tests pass. I then reinstalled all 14 apps so each has the updated copy.

**Docs.** Bilko's `CLAUDE.md` has a host-kit section: where it lives, which apps use it, the rebuild-and-reinstall steps after a change, and the Tailwind line apps need. My earlier edit to it never actually ran because a safety hook blocked that command, so this is new.

**Left alone:** uncommitted work in Etch, Fizzpop, MindSwiffer and Stack-Audit, including Etch's version bump.

**Not published:** none of these apps were republished to bilko.run. The live sites keep their old builds, including the old contrast and the missing badge background, until each one is published again.
